title: Genitive 4: 'There Is No X' Across All Genders
description: The нет + genitive construction works the same way for all three genders. Today you mix masculine, feminine, and neuter together.
descriptionRussian: Конструкция нет + родительный падеж работает одинаково для всех родов. Сегодня смешиваем мужской, женский и средний.
intro: Three lessons, three genders, and now no more warnings about which one is coming. The construction has not changed since lesson 1. What changes is that you have to work out the gender before you can produce the ending, and that is exactly the step that gets skipped when you practice one gender at a time.
rules: The нет + genitive construction works the same way for all three genders. The trigger is always нет; the form depends on the noun's dictionary form.
Common subject frames: 'У X нет ___' (X doesn't have), 'В/На X нет ___' (there's no Y in/on X), 'Здесь нет ___' (there's no Y here).

When you see нет followed by a noun, identify the gender of the noun's dictionary form and apply the matching rule: masculine consonant + -а, feminine -а → -ы / -и, feminine -я → -и, neuter -о → -а, neuter -е → -я.
examples: В комнате нет окна. (There's no window in the room.) окно (neuter) → окна.
У Лены нет брата. (Lena doesn't have a brother.) брат (masc) → брата.
У Маши нет книги. (Masha doesn't have a book.) книга (fem) → книги (spelling rule).
В холодильнике нет молока. (There's no milk in the fridge.) молоко (neuter) → молока.
У меня нет журнала. (I don't have a magazine.) журнал (masc) → журнала.

items.promptEnglish: There's no window in the room.
items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: neuter -о becomes which letter?
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 3: neuter nouns ending in -о swap -о for -а in the genitive. Окно → окна. The construction нет + genitive applies regardless of gender.

items.hint: Брат is masculine. Apply Lesson 1's rule.
items.explanation: Брат is masculine. The construction is the same as for neuter and feminine (нет triggers genitive), but the form follows the masculine rule: add -а → брата.

items.hint: Recall the spelling rule from Lesson 2.
items.explanation: Книга is feminine -а. The regular rule would give книгы, but the spelling rule writes -и instead of -ы after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч. So книга → книги.

items.promptEnglish: There's no milk in the fridge.
items.explanation: Молоко is neuter -о. Genitive: -о swaps to -а → молока. Notice that the construction is now 'В X нет ___' rather than 'У X нет ___,' but the case behavior is identical.
Машина is feminine ending in -а (no spelling-rule trigger). Genitive: -а → -ы → машины. The regular feminine pattern.

items.hint: First lesson's rule: masculine consonant + which ending?
items.explanation: Quick callback to Lesson 1: masculine consonant nouns add -а in the genitive. Журнал → журнала. By the end of this track this should feel automatic.

blanks: В стакане нет _____. (There's no water in the glass.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Вода is feminine ending in -а. Genitive: -а → -ы → воды. The construction 'В X нет ___' triggers genitive just like 'У X нет ___.'

errorCorrection.sentence: У Антона нет сын, только дочь.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Anton has no son, only a daughter.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. Сын is masculine animate; the genitive adds -а: сына. The 'two-clause' structure 'нет X, только Y' is a common Russian way to contrast, and both X and Y need their proper case (here X is gen, Y is nom because дочь is the subject of an implicit есть).

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня нет яблоко на завтрак сегодня.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I don't have an apple for breakfast today.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. Яблоко is neuter (-о ending); the neuter genitive swaps -о → -а: яблока. The same -а appears on masculine genitives (журнал → журнала): different ending starting points, same destination vowel.

errorCorrection.sentence: У Лены нет сестра, и она всегда чувствует это.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Lena has no sister, and she always feels it.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. Сестра is feminine ending in -а; the genitive swaps -а → -ы: сестры. The stem-final -р is a 'normal' consonant (not k/g/x/sh/zh/shch/ch), so the spelling rule does NOT kick in here; -ы stays as -ы.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня нет телефон в моей комнате.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I don't have a phone in my room.
errorCorrection.explanation: After нет the noun must shift into the genitive. Masculine consonant nouns add -а: телефон → телефона. Leaving the noun in the nominative is the most common mistake learners make with нет; Russian requires the genitive here.

errorCorrection.sentence: У Маши нет ручкы, чтобы писать письмо.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha has no pen to write the letter with.
errorCorrection.explanation: Feminine -а would normally swap to -ы (ручкы), but Russian's spelling rule blocks -ы after к, г, х, ж, ш, щ, ч. The correct form is ручки. The form 'ручкы' is not valid Russian; it's exactly the trap the spelling rule exists to catch.

errorCorrection.sentence: В классе нет место для нового стола.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: There's no room in the classroom for a new table.
errorCorrection.explanation: Neuter -о swaps to -а in the genitive: место → места. The construction 'В X нет Y' is parallel to 'У X нет Y'; both trigger the genitive on Y for any gender.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: There is a window in the room.
minimalPairs.explanation: After есть the noun stays in the nominative: окно. The genitive form окна appears in 'В комнате нет окна' (There's no window in the room). The same есть/нет contrast you saw in Lessons 1 and 2 holds for neuter as well.
After нет the noun shifts into the genitive. The regular rule would give книгы, but the spelling rule converts -ы to -и after к, г, х, ш, ж, щ, ч. So книга → книги.

reviewVocab.definition: gender (grammatical category: masculine, feminine, or neuter)
reviewVocab.example: В русском языке три рода: мужской, женский и средний.
